Thanks for the list. Looping in Ben (commercial lead), Naomi (finance) and Karthik (legal) to confirm positions and propose redline language. High-level answers to start:
• Pricing staircase: our standard is prospective pricing at the start of the next billing period; however, we can make retroactive true-ups for annual reconciliations on multi-period commits — can propose explicit language.
• Unused commits: default is forfeiture at year-end unless parties agree to a carry-forward clause (we can offer a one-time rollover for Year 1 as a concession).
• VAT: we typically invoice net and charge taxes where Redwood is required to collect; when the customer is responsible for VAT remittance we accept a gross-up clause to avoid double taxation.

Finance comment on tax and invoicing flows:
• VAT treatment: we can issue invoices net of taxes and include a tax line. If SilverPeak is the remitting party, we require a customer tax indemnity and evidence of tax registration to avoid charging VAT.

• Payment terms: Net 45 is fine but if SilverPeak needs Net 60 we should bake an early-payment discount or adjust pricing to account for extension.
